resolution.note: Resolved at design level. Sections 3.6-3.8 now apply the earlier absolute/continuous-clock deadline to signer, issuer and owned masters, include sleep, preserve same-boot anchors, and fail closed on TIME_UNCERTAIN. Runner budgets use the conservative exchange below. Destination clock error is explicitly unmeasured, not a finite verified bound. Section 9.3 retains A08, native wake/lifecycle and runner tests as open; this is not runtime verification.

Sections 3.4 and 5.3 replace lost-counter dependence with OS-CSPRNG 64-bit serials, explicitly disclose probabilistic collisions, and no longer reconstruct issuance history from the key backup. Unknown history remains unknown/unbounded. This accepts the probabilistic serial design already accepted in round 2, not a mathematical uniqueness guarantee; the key-only-restore test remains not_started.

Sections 3.6-3.7 (lines 317-360, 409-432) persist boot ID, continuous reading and trusted wall time per grant; same-boot restart resumes the original budget and cannot rebuild it from the wall clock. After reboot, high-water consistency AND synchronized time are required, otherwise TIME_UNCERTAIN. Owner-present time confirmation cannot move absolute deadlines or extend a surviving budget. This follows the supplied authority ruling. OS synchronization sources are candidates, expressly awaiting platform evidence (section 9.3 lines 975-976); their naming is not accepted as proof of a trustworthy time bound.

Section 3.6 (lines 365-384) binds the controller time response to a nonce over the authenticated pairing channel. Using T_c plus the entire measured RTT as the receipt-time upper bound subtracts transit uncertainty rather than adding delivery time. The deadline is retained per grant, later exchanges can only shorten it, and reboot requires a fresh exchange. Absent a bounded offset, TIME_UNCERTAIN prevents signing/admission under the common rule and owned masters are unavailable; credential_only describes the remaining server validity enforcement. Sections 7.2 and 9.3 propagate the conditions and delayed/replayed-delivery tests. This is a design argument assuming accepted controller time and the specified continuous clocks, not an executed exchange or measured drift bound.

Section 5.3 (lines 666-687) and section 6.2 explicitly report unknown/unbounded residuals after key-only restore unless a verified durable historical maximum covering every possibly outstanding certificate is recovered; V1 defines no such record. Current/saved policies and defaults are expressly forbidden as substitute bounds. Rotation is recommended; residual closure is per account after removal of the old trust line, with unreachable accounts remote_pending. Existing sessions/processes remain subject to the separate unbounded limits in section 6.2. Section 9.3 includes the old-long-certificate/shorter-restored-policy counterexample.

Section 3.5 (lines 228-245) reapplies every refusal predicate at publication using current time, including time confidence, state, effective deadline, cutoff, parent deadline and revisions. Failure voids without release. Installation separately checks the receiving signer's generation, tombstones and safe deadline; discarded published entries still count in residuals. Section 9.3 line 974 adds deadline/cutoff passage without edits and time-confidence failures across the protocol. Previously published credentials on disconnected runners retain the disclosed remote_pending residual; this does not promise instantaneous remote revocation.

summary: 6 resolved, 0 partly, 0 not; 0 new blockers/majors/minors requiring correction before M03. Accept revision 3 as a design specification under the supplied orchestrator rulings. Independent static review of ADR, normative spec/plan and G04 records only: no implementation, native lifecycle, synchronization signal or runner exchange was executed.
